Daily Digest · Computer Science

Robots Learn to Reason and Act Safely

Today's submissions reveal a maturing ecosystem where robots move beyond scripted behaviors into learned reasoning. From LLM-guided manipulation to safe flow matching with feasibility constraints, the field is tackling the hard problem of coupling perception, planning, and safety. The throughline: embodied AI systems that can generalize across tasks while respecting physical reality.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
Robotics
LLM Supervisors Distilled into Fast Decision Trees

Instead of querying expensive LLMs every time a robot encounters an anomaly, researchers distill the supervisor online into a decision tree using counterfactual replay. This cuts latency and cost dramatically while preserving reasoning capability.

Counterfactual labels retire unhelpful rules, enabling real-time supervised recovery decisions without continuous LLM calls.
Ceder, Freitag, Åkesson 2610.39775 PDF
Computer Vision
Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception in One Model

GenSight merges future video generation and dense perception—depth, segmentation, optical flow—into a single pretrained diffusion transformer. A shared DiT backbone with lightweight task modulation predicts all modalities jointly, enabling embodied world models that both imagine and perceive.

All tasks trained jointly on a unified spatiotemporal representation without separate supervision branches.
Feng, Liu, Wang 2610.39232 PDF
Machine Learning
Training-Free Non-Myopic Guidance for Safe Generation

AegisFlow steers diffusion and flow-matching models toward constrained outputs—identity preservation, obstacle avoidance—without retraining. It replaces myopic min-norm controllers with non-myopic guidance that plans ahead in constraint space.

Path-safe guidance that looks beyond immediate constraints, yielding safer and higher-quality trajectories at inference time.
Liu, Zhang, You 2610.39825 PDF
AI Safety
Safe Flow Matching via Black-Box Feasibility Oracles

Robot policies trained with flow matching can violate physical constraints. This work adds an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard that queries black-box feasibility oracles to correct unsafe updates in real time, enabling practical safe policy generation.

Binary feasibility queries suffice to constrain flow-based action generation without analytical descriptions of the feasible set.
Ma, Jin, Chen, Gao 2610.40075 PDF

Teaching a Tree to Recover: Online Distillation of an LLM Supervisor

Autonomous robots freeze in complex layouts when global planners and local MPC controllers disagree. This work distills an LLM supervisor into a decision tree online using counterfactual replay, enabling fast, cheap supervisory decisions without querying the LLM each time.

LLM-guided Planar Loco-Manipulation for Quadruped Robots

Cluttered environments often require physical interaction with movable obstacles to reach goals. A language-conditioned task planner jointly selects the skill, object, and geometric target, generalizing beyond predefined action sets or low-dimensional commands.

03
Understanding Axial Attention in TSFMs Through Single Location Regression

Time Series Foundation Models rely on axial attention but its theory is sparse. This work extends the Single Location Regression framework to 2D data, proving statistical properties and training dynamics of axial attention in sparse information settings.

cs.AIcs.LGPantea, DieuleveutPDF
04
Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles

Flow-based robot policies lack guarantees on physical constraints. An oracle-guided differentiable safeguard uses binary feasibility queries to correct unsafe updates, enabling constraint satisfaction when the feasible set is unknown or non-analytical.

cs.ROcs.AIMa, Jin, Chen, GaoPDF
05
LiDAR-SHIELD: Adversarial Robustness Framework for 3D Perception

LiDAR-based 3D models in autonomous systems need robustness testing. LIDAR-SHIELD unifies fragmented adversarial attack implementations into a Dockerized framework, removing friction in stress-testing different architectures and tasks.

AegisFlow: Training-Free Non-Myopic Path-Safe Guided Flow Matching

Steering generative models toward constrained outputs—identity preservation, obstacle avoidance—typically requires retraining. AegisFlow enables non-myopic guidance at inference that plans ahead in constraint space without any additional training.

07
Seeing and Imagining as One: Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception

Embodied world models need to imagine plausible futures and perceive geometric structure. GenSight unifies video generation and dense perception—depth, segmentation, flow—in one pretrained diffusion transformer with task-specific modulation.

08
CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse Alignment

Retrieving 3D scenes or objects from 2D queries requires learning dense alignments, not just scene-level supervision. Sparse 2D-3D correspondences alone suffice to train one model for both scene and instance-level retrieval tasks.

Agentic LLM Reasoning in Pediatric Diabetes Outcome Prediction

Predicting rare clinical outcomes in small pediatric cohorts is hard; LLMs are untested here. CEDAR, an evidence-citing self-auditing LLM pipeline, outperforms trained ML on seven outcomes from multimodal medical records spanning 6,500+ youth.

Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment via Value of Information

Robot memory systems face two costs: expensive attention over large stores and credit assignment across long sequences. A learned world model estimates value of information to enable cheap retrieval and provable credit bounds without computing full attention.

Attention, Dynamic Wave and Hybrid Sequence Mixers in Language Models

Scaling LLMs to long contexts is hampered by quadratic attention cost. A formalised Dynamic Wave recurrent layer with exponential damping and phase modulation, tested in hybrid and pure configurations on TinyStories, reaches competitive perplexity at lower latency.

ROAD: Modern Adversarial Training for Simple One-Step Distillation

One-step diffusion distillation at text-to-image scale has struggled with pure adversarial training. ROAD proposes a lightweight representation-space critic with Lipschitz-controlled Transformer head, simplifying machinery while scaling to modern models.

Joint Rigid Alignment and Morphable Reconstruction from Partial 3D Faces

Aligning partial real-world 3D face scans requires solving two coupled problems: rigid pose estimation and shape completion. Built on GeoTransformer, a single network predicts both simultaneously, replacing decoupled registration and deformation pipelines.

AVPS-360: Spatial Audio-Visual Benchmark for Person Segmentation

Existing audio-visual instance segmentation benchmarks use monaural audio, losing spatial cues. AVPS-360 pairs first-order Ambisonics with 360° video across 230 recordings, bridging audio-visual segmentation and sound event localization.

IMPACT: Physics-Informed Multimodal Learning for PV Forecasting

Solar power forecasting at 10–110 minute horizons requires fusing temporal plant history, spatial cloud dynamics, solar geometry, and meteorology. A four-branch architecture with gated cross-attention and physics-grounded signals delivers probabilistic forecasts.

EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On

LLM-based computer-use agents face environments that change mid-task—appointments move, policies shift. EnvOS certifies that task changes fire correctly and tracks agent failures to their root cause: agent error, unexecuted change, or grading failure.

It Takes Two to Probe, Thousands to Retrieve: Vision-Language Evaluation

Vision-language probing benchmarks test fine-grained understanding with handcrafted negatives; real retrieval beats thousands. Comparing these methods on SugarCrepe and SVOQA shows handcrafted probes don't predict retrieval rank robustly.

SynthFaces: Balanced Large Scale Human Dataset

Real face datasets are biased and privacy-risky, harming fair generative models. A controllable generation pipeline expands Arc2Face diffusion to create diverse, balanced synthetic faces for training identity-preserving generative models.

Coupled Guidance for Flow Matching

Flow-matching guidance lags behind diffusion despite structural parallels. Theoretical analysis reveals instability in naive adaptations; coupled guidance provides a stable framework for steering stochastic controllers and controlled image synthesis.

Don't Risk It: Trajectory-Conditioned Distributional Risk

Crowd navigation without fragile tracking requires anticipating collision-free space. DRIP, an LiDAR-only planner, forecasts occupancy and predicts clearance distributions for candidate trajectories, grounding uncertainty in empirical collision data.

UniRA: Unified Representation Alignment and Auto-Encoding

DiTs train slowly and cost heavily. UniRA unifies Representation Alignment and Representation Auto-Encoders, applying both alignment of intermediate features and representation-space tokenization to accelerate training and reduce compute.

H²R: Hierarchical Hint-Based Reward for Mathematical Reasoning

RL with verifiable rewards improves LLM math, but lacks intermediate supervision for multi-step problems. H²R uses the intrinsic sub-question structure of problems as hierarchical hints, grounding intermediate milestones logically.

TACFormer: Transformer-Based PROTAC Design via Generative Modeling

Drug discovery via targeted protein degradation relies on PROTACs, but design is trial-and-error. A transformer-based generative model explores PROTAC chemical space in silico, conditionally generating candidates and enabling virtual screening.

sDMD: Sinkhorn Distribution Matching Distillation

Distribution Matching Distillation distills diffusion into few-step generators, but guidance by local density causes mode collapse. Connecting DMD to Wasserstein gradient flow and proposing Sinkhorn-based matching preserves mode coverage.

Exploring Symbolic Regression in Precision Livestock Farming

Predicting farrowing time from sow acceleration sensors needs both accuracy and interpretability. Symbolic regression delivers explainable models that balance piglet safety and sow welfare, addressing the 'closed-box' problem of traditional ML.

Featured Researcher
KC
Kristian Ceder
Robotics Researcher · Chalmers University

Ceder's work bridges classical control and modern LLMs, specializing in how autonomous systems can leverage language models without the computational overhead. His distillation approach—converting expensive supervisors into efficient decision trees—addresses a key bottleneck in real-world robotics. Featured today for demonstrating practical scaling of learned supervision on mobile platforms.
